At Sandvik Rock Tools in Sandviken, we're exploring how industrial sensor data can provide earlier and more reliable insight into machine conditions. This thesis combines practical measurements on production equipment with signal processing, data analysis, and AI to establish a reusable approach for future condition-monitoring initiatives. Background and purpose Modern production equipment generates many signals, but existing machine data is not always reliable or sampled at the frequency required for condition assessment. Additional sensors may be needed to capture vibration, temperature, acoustic, electrical, pressure, or other process-related phenomena.  The purpose of this thesis is to evaluate suitable sensors and data-collection methods, then analyze data from selected equipment using statistical and AI-based methods. The result should support further development of condition monitoring, diagnostics, and data-driven maintenance at Rock Tools. Work description The thesis is carried out as a structured proof of concept. Together with the company supervisor, you refine the scope, machine case, and success criteria. The work is expected to include:     Review relevant research on industrial condition monitoring, sensor selection, signal processing, and AI methods.     Define machine states, operating conditions, potential failure modes, and evaluation criteria.     Evaluate sensors and data-acquisition solutions based on sampling rate, installation, synchronization, robustness, accessibility and cost.     Plan and perform data collection, documenting sensor placement, machine settings and data quality.     Clean, synchronize and analyze time-series data using suitable time, frequency or time-frequency features.     Develop and compare statistical baselines and AI models for classification or anomaly detection.     Validate performance, including false alarms, missed detections, changing operating conditions, explainability and uncertainty.     Recommend sensors, an architecture aligned with the Sandvik Rock Tools Unified Namespace, a modelling approach and next steps. Expected deliverables are a sensor and data-acquisition concept, a quality-checked dataset, reproducible analysis and model code, a comparison of methods and a roadmap for continued development. The objective is a robust proof of concept and reusable method, not a production-ready predictive-maintenance platform.   Your profile We're looking for one or two analytical and hands-on students with an interest in industrial equipment, measurement technology, and data science. You work systematically, document decisions, and connect model results to physical machine behavior. Your background includes:     Ongoing Master’s studies in automation, mechatronics, mechanical or electrical engineering, engineering physics, computer science, industrial data science or a related field.     Experience with Python and data analysis.      An understanding of, or motivation to learn, time-series analysis, signal processing, machine learning and experimental design.       Good communication skills in English; Swedish is advantageous.  Experience with vibration analysis, industrial sensors, OPC UA, MQTT, PLC/CNC data or condition monitoring is advantageous, as is Knowledge of NumPy, pandas, SciPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch or TensorFlow. Our culture At Sandvik, we work with advanced technology and exciting innovations, but our people are the key to our success. We believe diversity and inclusion create stronger results through mutual support, knowledge sharing and different perspectives. Visit our stories hub, LinkedIn or Facebook to get to know us further.  Scope The thesis corresponds to 30 ECTS credits and approximately 20 weeks of full-time work. The start date is agreed with the selected student or students and the university.  The position is based at Rock Tools in Sandviken, Sweden, with access to relevant equipment, data and supervision. Confidentiality, data handling and publication boundaries will be agreed at the start of the project. Contact information For more information, please contact Andreas Nelson, Method Development, at Tools, andreas.nelson@sandvik.comWe’ve already decided on which advertising channels and marketing campaigns we wish to use and respectfully decline any additional contacts in that matter. Application Please submit your application by December 13, 2026. Attach your CV, cover letter and transcript of records. Describe your experience with sensor data, signal processing, machine learning or industrial equipment, and what interests you most about the project. Applications by email are not accepted. Job ID: R0099692. Sandvik is a global, high-tech engineering group providing solutions that enhance productivity, profitability and sustainability in the manufacturing, mining and infrastructure industries. Our offering includes equipment, tools, services and digital solutions for machining, mining, rock excavation, crushing and screening.

Research shows that women and other under-represented groups within our industry hesitate to apply unless they tick most boxes of a role description. At Stegra, we are building an impact company with sustainability at its core. We need a diverse, inclusive, and authentic team to rally behind our purpose of de-carbonizing hard-to-abate industries, starting with steel.So, if you are equally passionate about our purpose yet concerned that your experience doesn’t perfectly align with the qualifications stated in the job advert, we strongly encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate, either for this role – or for another upcoming role in our rapidly growing business.About us:Stegra is on a mission to disrupt the global steel industry by producing green steel, with the end goal of bringing down CO2 emissions to zero. By using green hydrogen and fossil-free electricity instead of coal; water and heat will be our primary emissions. By 2030, our ambition is to produce 5 million tonnes of green steel annually in our fully integrated, digitalized, and sustainable plant in Boden, located in northern Sweden - currently in construction phase. But this is just the beginning – our expertise in green hydrogen will enable us to decarbonize other industries in addition to steel, and we look forward to what’s next in store for us.We are looking for talented, innovative, and purpose-driven people to join our rapidly growing and diverse team. Coordinate preparation and release of groundworks scopes, ensuring drawings, quantities, and execution requirements are ready for construction    Maintain the Groundworks Scope Tracker and consolidate inputs from EPCM partners, design teams, and planners    Support forecasting and planning of upcoming groundworks activities    Coordinate scope clarifications between Engineering, Planning, Construction, and contractors    Support and maintain a structured RFI process between contractors and engineering stakeholders    Help align groundworks activities with project schedules, civil milestones, and interface dependencies    Participate in coordination meetings and support progress reporting and issue resolution    Monitor contractor readiness, access conditions, and documentation prior to site executionWhat you’ll bringYou’re curious and believe that real progress happens when we work together. jobs.occupation: Software Engineer - Machine Learning or Computer Vision
jobs.description: Volumental is the footwear industry’s leading FitTech™ company, using 3D scanning and machine learning to match people with shoes that truly fit.Our vision is “a world without sizes, where every body fits.” We work with brands such as New Balance, Red Wing, Fleet Feet, and Vivobarefoot across 3,000+ stores in 60 countries, with 60M+ foot scans collected, one of the world’s largest datasets of its kind.Computer vision, machine learning, and AI have always been at the core of our product. Today, we also use AI agents as everyday companions in our work, helping us shorten feedback cycles, deepen our expertise, and explore new areas. We believe the best work comes from people who never stop learning and who care deeply about their craft.Our Products and TeamsWe target businesses and stores selling footwear such as shoes, ski boots and hockey skates, as well as insoles. We develop two related products, each with its own team:    In-store product. We sell a 3D scanner that our business customers put in their physical retail stores and use to scan shoppers' feet. The scanner is controlled by a tablet, which shows the 3D scans and recommends footwear from the store's range.    Online product. We sell 3D scanning and recommendation web components that our business customers integrate into their online store. It allows online shoppers to scan their own feet using their own phone and get size recommendations for the footwear in that online store.We are also exploring new product opportunities, such as 3D scanning beyond feet and footwear. You will start in our Online product team, with the chance to move into other teams over time. Whichever team you are in, you will be part of shaping our current and future products. Algorithm Development at VolumentalBoth of our products are built on top of two core algorithmic systems:    3D foot scanning system. It takes images of a person's feet and reconstructs a 3D model. This involves areas such as camera calibration, image processing, image classification, image segmentation, object detection, parametric 3D models, numerical optimization and machine learning.    Footwear recommendation system. This is based on machine learning and our ever-growing dataset of more than 30 million samples of 3D scans matched with footwear purchases. Given a shopper's unique pair of feet, we predict and recommend what footwear will fit them. This involves areas such as machine learning, probabilistic methods, model fitting, numerical optimization, training, inference, ranking, statistics, data visualization, data cleaning and outlier detection.For both systems, we put a strong emphasis on empirical evaluation and optimization, based on data that we continuously gather from our users. We want to measure what works and what does not (yet) work in practice, and find ways to improve it.You will have the chance to work on either of these systems, depending partly on your previous experience and interests and partly on the current needs of our products and users.Our algorithmic tech stack includes technologies like: Python, C++, Go, SQL, NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, Polars, TensorFlow, Keras, JAX, Eigen, Ceres, OpenCV, Google Cloud Platform, BigQuery, Devin AI, Greptile, Claude… You will influence which tools we use, and if you find something better, we want to hear about it. We offer premium AI agent subscriptions and encourage everyone to explore, test, and share useful ways of working with AI. We are excited about you because you:    Have experience in both mathematical modeling and programming.    Are a collaborative and kind team member.    Can solve difficult problems in practice.    Have experience working with datasets and evaluating different methods.    Have a master's degree in computer science, engineering physics, electrical engineering, or similar.It is a plus if you:    Have professional experience of software engineering.    Have professional experience working with algorithms in areas like:    Machine learning    Computer vision    Computer graphics    Image processing    Robotics    Numerical optimization What we can offer you:    Personal learning budget and access to coaching    Opportunity to work with a great team of 15+ nationalities in our English-speaking office    Occupational pension at ITP1 level    Flexible Public Holidays Policy    Options Program    Parental pay top-up    Wellness allowance    Flexible work policy (at least 3 days a week from our Stockholm office) The monthly compensation range for this role in Stockholm is 50,000-77,000 SEK. Actual compensation will depend on level, experience, and skillset as assessed in the interview process.We are hiring for multiple positions and welcome both junior and senior engineers from all backgrounds. We’d love to hear from you!

jobs.description: Job ID: 7501(Senior) Quantitative Analyst, Model Monitoring and Performance (permanent position)Are you a quantitative analyst with a knack for navigating complex databases and producing clear analysis? Do you have knowledge of credit risk processes and an interest in, or experience with, IRB, IFRS9 or similar models? Then this opportunity may be for you! Quantitative Analyst to join the Model Monitoring and Performance team (MMP) within Risk Models.Nordea are currently developing and implementing a suite of new, state-of-the-art IRB and IFRS9 models. MMP is responsible for ensuring that the new models’ performance is continuously scrutinized, and for identifying any issues arising within them. Further, we are responsible for assessing and overseeing how IRB models are used in credit processes, including whether model use is in line with regulations, internal requirements and the approved purpose of the models.Our key stakeholders are model developers, model users in Business and senior management. About our teamMeet the Model Monitoring and Performance team. Our role is to contribute to assessments of how IRB models are used in credit processes, communicate identified issues and help develop clear internal guidelines for appropriate model use.Our team is an inspiring, competent and creative group of professionals in an international environment. In your daily job, you’ll be applying your quantitative and data analysis skills to produce clear and concise communication about model performance and performance issues to model developers and senior management. You’ll mainly be working with Python, SQL and Snowflake, but SAS and other tools may be used here and there. The role will be located in Helsinki or Stockholm and team colleagues are in Stockholm, Helsinki and Copenhagen.Collaboration. Ownership. Passion. Courage. These are the values that guide us in how we work and how we make decisions – and that we imagine you share with us. What you’ll be doingMain responsibilities in this role:    Quantitative analysis of model performance for all components of IRB and/or IFRS9 models (PD, LGD, EAD).    Communicating conclusions of your analysis to model developers and senior management – in reports and meetings.    Developing, maintaining and operating the IRB and IFRS9 model performance monitoring frameworks.    Collaborating with a variety of stakeholders including risk management, model development, model validation and model users across the bank.    Assessing how IRB models are used in credit processes, identifying potential gaps against regulatory and internal requirements, and communicating conclusions and follow-up needs.Who you areThis is the right role for you if you:    Are driven by a desire to know more.    Love to make sense of data.    Are self-driven and take ownership.    Find it easy to understand others, and make yourself understood by others.    Love to think in terms of the big picture, but know that the devil is in the details.    Enjoy learning, and are excited about bringing your ideas to the table.    Are honest and reliable, and willing to speak up even when it’s difficult.    Think it is important to get governance right.Your background and skills include:    Master’s in a quantitative field such as mathematics, engineering, econometrics, data science, finance, or similar.    Excellent communication skills (English is the working language).    Sound knowledge of applied mathematical modelling and excellent quantitative skills.    Proficiency in Python and SQL.    Knowledge of credit risk processes and how risk models and parameters are used in credit assessment and decision-making.    Knowledge of or interest in IRB, IFRS9 or similar models – practical experience with model use, monitoring or governance is a definitive plus.What we offerPeople come here when they want to get somewhere. For some, it’s to take their career to the next level. For others, it’s to break new ground within their area of expertise – in other words, with us, you will always move forward.A culture that fosters performance and growth in one of the largest Nordic banks, offering various opportunities to evolve, develop and learn from brilliant colleagues with diverse backgrounds in a vibrant working environment.Hybrid working model – we believe in the value of bringing people together and at the same time we embrace the freedom of flexibility.Diversity and inclusion are a natural part of our daily work. We know that an inclusive workplace is a sustainable one. We genuinely believe that our diverse backgrounds, experiences, characteristics and traits make us stronger together. Every day we strive to find new ways to improve diversity and inclusion within our community e.g. we have signed the European Diversity Charters in the countries where we operate to show our commitment and engage with others to continue learning and improving.If this sounds like you, get in touch!Next stepsSubmit your application no later than 03/12/2026.For more information, you’re welcome to contact Rene Eriksen at rene.eriksen@nordea.com.We enable dreams and aspirations for a greater good.We build relationships. We add a personal touch to everything we do – when advising our customers, collaborating with colleagues, and meeting our potential candidates.We learn and develop. We take pride in being experts and thinking ahead. We use our expertise to meet our customers’ needs, from the simplest to the most complex. We bring a growth mindset to our work that enables us to focus on a broader perspective in our daily challenges.We lead change. We are responsible and aware of the impact of our decisions, both for our customers and for our local and global communities. Mindful of our responsibility towards current and future generations, we have made sustainability an integrated part of our business strategy.We are Nordea. We have a 200-year history of supporting and growing the Nordic economies and our values are deeply rooted in these open, progressive and collaborative societies. As one of the biggest employers in the Nordics, Poland and Estonia, you have excellent opportunities to evolve, develop and move forward with us.If you are an external consultant interested in this role and wish to apply please contact the hiring people leader for separate instruction on how to apply.Only for candidates in Sweden: For union information, please contact Finansförbundet at finansforbundet@nordea.se or SACO at SacoNordea@nordea.com.
